brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: stratified earth-toned sidebar literally maps spending depth to geological layers, reinforced by labels like Topsoil/Bedrock.
Warm sand/ochre palette feels coherent with the geology theme and contrasts nicely with the cool blue progress and CTA accents.
Depth Analysis panel extends the metaphor into insights (Erosion Risk, Core Stability), giving the concept reflective payoff.
dominant_weaknesses: Sidebar amounts use a stray 'M' suffix ($420M, $1,780M) which reads as millions and breaks credibility for personal spending.
The blue progress bars and blue 'Add to Layer' button feel imported from a generic dashboard kit, clashing with the earthy stratigraphy concept.
Hierarchy is flat: category cards, transaction rows, and the form all share similar weight, so the eye has no clear entry point.
fix_priorities: Remove the 'M' suffix or replace with subtle depth indicators (meters of layer thickness tied to budget share).
Recolor progress bars and primary button into the earth palette (rust, clay, slate) to unify with the metaphor.
Strengthen typographic hierarchy — larger category headers, lighter transaction meta, distinct treatment for the sidebar layer names.
Introduce subtle texture or stratification gradient between layers to make the geological cross-section more visceral.
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept leads, visceral execution is pleasant but behavioral clarity suffers from flat hierarchy and ambiguous numeric units.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the geological-layer metaphor for necessity vs discretionary spending is clearly and creatively expressed, though execution details dilute the idea.
